_about: Requested state for GET https://api.eu1.notabene.id/entity/did:web:citi.com:test:us/public-keys , which today returns 404 NO_ENCRYPTION_KEYS. The key below is ours: we hold the private half and it never leaves our infrastructure, which is what makes the PII exchange end-to-end rather than Notabene-managed.
_reference: Shaped to match a working sandbox entity, did:web:delubacfr-efe52.sandbox.notabene.id:fr , whose /public-keys response is byte-identical to the #notabene-pii entry in its published DID document. We verified that match, so we assume /public-keys is served from the DID document and that publishing the entry below is what produces this response.

didDocumentChange._note: Add this entry to verificationMethod and add its id to keyAgreement. Please KEEP the existing #notabene-pii entry so anything already in flight still decrypts; '#pii' outranks '#notabene-pii' in your key-selection order, so /public-keys will return ours.

alternativeEncoding._note: The same key as EcdsaSecp256r1VerificationKey2019 + publicKeyHex, if that shape suits your pipeline better. Compressed SEC1 P-256 point.

alsoRequested: Publish this entity's DID document at a location that resolves. did:web:citi.com:test:us resolves per the did:web method to https://citi.com/test/us/did.json , which returns 404 - we do not control citi.com. Delubac's sandbox entity sits under *.sandbox.notabene.id and resolves. Either re-provision ours the same way, or tell us the exact URL you expect us to serve.

Confirm what raises a REQUIRE_PRESENTATION policy on a sandbox transfer. Transfers we create from did:web:citi.com:test:us naming did:web:citi.com:test:il as beneficiary VASP are not visible to that entity at all, and come back with empty policyEvaluations.
Confirm our tenant is Transact V2 and that /entities/{did}/tx plus /presentation is the correct integration path for these DIDs.
